senses.gloss: m. (נָפַח; cmp. מַפַּח נפש) fainting, decay; disappointment.—ת׳ נפש, ת׳ רוח, (Chald. ת׳ רוחא) let fainting come upon …, let despair come upon …! R. Hash. 31ᵃ ששה … אמרה ת׳ נפשם וכ׳ Ms. M. (ed. אמר ת׳ עצמן, read: עצמותן) the Shechinah delayed six months in the desert for Israel’s sake, perhaps they would return in repentance: when they did not return, the Shechinah said, let despair come upon them &c. (ref. to Job XI, 20 מפח נפש …).
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 105b:14">Keth. 105ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ נפשם של וכ׳</he> oh, the despair that waits for those who take bribes! <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 4:6:9">Y. Maas. Sh. IV, 55ᵇ</cite> bot. [read:] <he>ת׳ רוחיה דהאי גברא</he> woe to that man! <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7:4">Num. R. s. 7<sup>4</sup></cite> (to a plant) <he>ת׳ רוחך וכ׳</he> woe to thee! last night thou wast looking well &c., v. <cite ref="Q01546"><he>פָּרַג</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 3:12">Ex. R. s. 3<sup>12</sup></cite> <he>ת׳ עצמותה</he> (read: <he>עצמותיה</he>) Oh, the decay of her bones, woe to her!; a. fr.
